record.title: ScholarStack reports cross-task reuse of layered scientific research assets
record.summary: A September 2026 preprint describes a research-asset framework that keeps source-grounded paper statements, domain organization and scoped cross-paper syntheses as distinct but linked objects. Across four task families, the authors report that gains concentrate on multi-paper evidence tasks and that query-time token use falls where measured. On a 797-question multi-paper QA set, the paper reports a higher five-dimension score than its full-text baseline while using fewer generation tokens. Construction and judging costs are excluded from that comparison; results are author-reported and rely on benchmark- and judge-specific methods.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The authors define three linked asset layers: source-grounded paper facts with conditions and evidence references; domain organization; and scoped cross-paper syntheses with coverage and supporting or limiting evidence.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: On 797 MDAQA questions using the same answering model, the paper reports an 18.41 score versus 8.46 for full-text across five scored dimensions, and 5.5k versus 20.8k generation tokens per question. The score is a sum of judge-scored dimensions; usage excludes asset construction and judging.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: Across four task families and ten task settings, the authors report that quality gains concentrate on tasks needing cross-paper evidence and query-time token costs fall where measured. These are the authors’ benchmark results, not independent evidence of general superiority or total end-to-end savings.

evidence_gaps.description: The reported query-token reduction excludes the one-time construction of research assets and judging costs; the end-to-end break-even point and update/revision costs are not established.

The paper’s multi-task results are author-reported; no public implementation, frozen asset collection or independent reproduction was inspected. Some benchmark conditions use constructed gold and LLM-based judging.

brief.importance_rationale: If the reported cross-task gains generalize, preserving evidence-linked research assets could materially change scientific-agent workflows and reduce repeated context processing. A 6 reflects results across several task settings, bounded by author-run studies, constructed assets/benchmarks and excluded construction costs.
limitations: The accessible evidence is an author preprint and has not been independently reproduced.
Quality results vary by task; gains are reported as concentrated on cross-paper evidence tasks rather than universal.
The 797-question QA score is a five-dimension sum produced under the paper’s evaluation protocol; results are judge- and dataset-dependent.
Query-time token comparisons exclude construction and judging costs, so they do not establish total cost savings.
Some appendices describe self-constructed benchmarks and single-judge or author-generated gold limitations.
brief.summary: A September 2026 preprint describes a research-asset framework that keeps source-grounded paper statements, domain organization and scoped cross-paper syntheses as distinct but linked objects. Across four task families, the authors report that gains concentrate on multi-paper evidence tasks and that query-time token use falls where measured. On a 797-question multi-paper QA set, the paper reports a higher five-dimension score than its full-text baseline while using fewer generation tokens. Construction and judging costs are excluded from that comparison; results are author-reported and rely on benchmark- and judge-specific methods.

technical.claimed_result: On 797 MDAQA questions the authors report 18.41 versus 8.46 on a five-dimension score and 5.5k versus 20.8k generation tokens per question; they also report cross-task quality gains and lower query costs where measured.
technical.demonstrated_result: The paper specifies matched model and source conditions for selected evaluations and reports results across four task families. Results remain author-reported and have not been independently reproduced in this activation.
technical.mechanism: A shared interface compiles source-grounded statements, domain-level organization and evidence-scoped cross-paper syntheses as versioned, provenance-linked assets; tasks request views at different evidence granularities.
technical.regime: Four task families, ten task settings; multi-paper QA on 797 MDAQA questions; token/time accounting excludes knowledge construction and judging.
technical.reproducibility: No independent implementation or reproduction was performed; public code or frozen assets were not inspected.
technical.strongest_baseline: Task-specific baselines including full-text under matched base models and, for selected conditions, matched source-paper collections and context budgets.

brief.title: ScholarStack reports cross-task reuse of layered scientific research assets
brief.why_it_matters: Research agents repeat source processing across retrieval, question answering, literature synthesis and claim checks. The paper evaluates whether retaining scoped, provenance-linked intermediate research assets can improve cross-paper tasks and reduce query-time work. Its evidence supports a bounded author-reported framework result, not a general claim that reusable assets always improve scientific work or total cost.
